# midpoint_object_template (Resource)

A midPoint object template (ObjectTemplateType): mappings and item definitions applied to focus objects.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A user template that computes fullName from givenName and familyName.
resource "midpoint_object_template" "user" {
  name            = "User template"
  description     = "Computes the full name of every user."
  lifecycle_state = "active"

  # A list of mappings; one mapping object is accepted too.
  mapping = [
    yamldecode(<<-EOT
      name: full-name
      strength: weak
      source:
        - path: givenName
        - path: familyName
      expression:
        script:
          code: "basic.concatName(givenName, familyName)"
      target:
        path: fullName
    EOT
    ),
  ]

  item = [{
    ref         = "description"
    displayName = "Description"
  }]

  iteration_specification = { maxIterations = 5 }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Object name.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) When an object with the configured oid already exists, adopt it into state and apply the configuration to it as an update instead of failing. The configuration must describe the whole object: items midPoint holds that are not configured (other than server-managed ones) are removed on the first apply. The plan warns that the object will be adopted and lists the changes the update will send. Meant for the midPoint built-ins a catalogue customizes. Without it, creating an object whose oid already exists fails and nothing is written. While it is true, destroying the object fails unless force_destroy is set: an adopted object is not Terraform's to delete. Remove it from state with a removed block (lifecycle { destroy = false }) to stop managing it. Importing a midPoint built-in (oid 00000000-0000-0000-0000-*) records it as adopted (true); any other import records false. Defaults to false.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `extra` (Dynamic) Other midPoint items, merged at the object root, in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. yamldecode(file("extra.yaml")). An item must not also be set by a typed attribute.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the object even when it was adopted with adopt_existing = true, which is refused otherwise. There is no reference check for this type. Defaults to false.
- `item` (Dynamic) Item definitions (item) in midPoint naming: a list, or one object. Always written, and read back after a change in midPoint, as a list.
- `iteration_specification` (Dynamic) Iteration specification (iterationSpecification) in midPoint naming, e.g. { maxIterations = 5 }.
- `lifecycle_state` (String) Lifecycle state (lifecycleState), e.g. active, draft, proposed.
- `mapping` (Dynamic) Template mappings (mapping) in midPoint naming: a list of mappings, or one mapping object. Always written, and read back after a change in midPoint, as a list.
- `oid` (String) Object OID. When unset midPoint generates one. Changing it replaces the object. Creating an object whose oid already exists fails unless adopt_existing is set.
- `options` (List of String) midPoint execution options sent on create and update, e.g. raw, isImport, reevaluateSearchFilters. When unset, the provider default_options entry for object_template applies, else the built-in defaults: isImport, raw on create and raw on update. An empty list sends no options. overwrite is sent only when listed here; reevaluateSearchFilters is added to any write that sends a reference with a filter and no oid.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The object OID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the object OID.
terraform import midpoint_object_template.user 10000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000222
```
